# 24Houring

> 24Houring (https://24houring.com) is a web app that visualizes a day as a
> 24-hour circular timetable (a clock-style pie chart), with a monthly
> calendar that can be decorated like a paper diary (다꾸). Users plan the day
> and the month, check tasks off, keep a daily log, and share the result as an
> image or link.
> The core planner is free with no sign-up: it runs client-side, stores data
> on-device, works offline, and supports 8 languages. An optional Pro plan
> (current price shown in the app and Polar checkout) adds cloud sync, end-to-end encryption, and push
> alarms. The site also hosts an extensive library of Korean/English articles
> on daily planning, plus ready-made templates and a design gallery.

## What it is

- A circular **24-hour day planner / timetable** ("생활계획표") that shows the
  whole day at a glance — the format Korean and Japanese children traditionally
  drew by hand for school-vacation plans, rebuilt as a web app.
- Also offers **12-hour clock views**: Day (06:00–18:00) and Night
  (18:00–06:00). All views edit the same underlying day.
- Edit by dragging time-block boundaries; split a block with one click
  (scissors) and merge by removing a divider. Blocks have names, colors and
  icons; tasks can be **checked off** and a daily completion rate is shown.
- Extras: multi-day schedules, a daily memo/diary, sticky notes, clock /
  calendar / weather / goals / news widgets, a decorate wizard, a
  line-art desktop pet, and per-slice start alarms.

## Monthly calendar and diary decorating (다꾸)

- **Calendar mode** (the “Calendar” button at the top, or
  https://24houring.com/?view=calendar): two months side by side, all-day /
  timed / multi-day plans (drag across dates), daily/weekly/monthly/yearly
  repeats with “this one / from here on / all” edits, five-week months whose
  overflow days open the next month’s first row. Free.
- **Google Calendar import** (Pro): a private iCal address added in
  ⚙ Settings → Connect Google Calendar shows those events read-only; the
  diary lock (end-to-end encryption passphrase) must be set first.
- **Diary-style decorating / 다이어리 꾸미기** (Design → Decorate calendar):
  colour themes (free); paper textures — grid, lined, dot, kraft; 300+ emoji
  stickers in 10 categories; masking tape in 5 patterns × 6 colours; polaroid
  photo stickers; a day highlighter (all Pro). Decorations are placed freely
  on a layer and stored relative to the month grid, so they keep their spot
  at any screen size. Photo pixels stay on the device that added them.
- **Calendar image export**: Export in calendar mode saves a 2160-px-wide PNG
  of a month with plans and decorations, or shares it from a phone. Free;
  drawn on the device, not uploaded.
- Landing page: https://24houring.com/calendar

## Life timeline (라이프 · 인생 타임라인)

- **Life mode** (the “Life” button at the top, or
  https://24houring.com/?view=life): the third time scale after the day and
  the month. A birthday alone draws one vertical line — birth, a label for
  every decade, today (age shown as full years) and a dashed stretch ahead.
  Nobody is asked how long they expect to live: the paper simply ends at 120.
  The page opens with today in the middle of the screen.
- Moments are dated to the year, month or day (year only → “about N”),
  may have an end date, a category with a colour and an icon (family,
  education, work, relationships, health, travel, achievement, home, other),
  a description and a photo (Pro). Dates after today are plans (dashed
  cards). Cards alternate left/right on wide screens; on phones they run to
  the right of a line on the left. Category filters, pinned moments, a
  summary line (records · plans · age · years ahead).
- **Several lives side by side**: a line can be added for anybody else —
  a parent, a child, the friend who was in the same city for three of those
  years — and they are drawn as columns against the same run of years, so a
  date shared by two of them sits at the same height on both. Names can be
  dragged into order, folded away, or let go. Free: two lines (mine and one
  other); Pro: up to ten.
- **Adding**: hover the line for a faint + circle that adds a moment where
  the line was pressed — the form opens on the month that point falls in (on
  phones: tap the line, or the + under today).
- **Where it happened**: a moment can name a city, which colours that country
  on the place map (below).
- **Words to leave behind**: an ending note where the line ends.
- **Export**: one tall PNG (2160 px wide) after a privacy check; a JSON
  backup (photos included) that restores on any device.
- Free: 30 moments and two lines, no photos; Pro: unlimited moments, ten
  lines, adding photos, sync. Photos stay on the device — never on the server,
  even with Pro. Limits only stop adding — nothing written is ever removed.
- Landing page: https://24houring.com/life

## Relation map (관계 · the people around you)

- **Relation mode** (the fourth tab, or https://24houring.com/?view=relation):
  me in the middle, and everybody who matters drawn around me. It is NOT a
  social network — there are no accounts but the owner's, no friend requests,
  no matching, no messages, and the other person is never told they are on
  somebody's map. A private note about the people in a life, kept on the
  device like everything else here.
- **Closeness is distance**: five rungs, and the rung IS how far out somebody
  is drawn (150 to 490 px from the middle). The group — family, friend, work,
  other — says which way from the middle; closeness says how far. The closest
  are drawn as the largest circles, in the heaviest line.
- **The map has weight**: the people repel each other, the ties pull, and each
  group is enclosed by a soft boundary with its name on it. It arranges
  itself when it opens, settles, and then drifts gently. Anybody can be
  dragged and put down where they are.
- **Ties between two people** (not only to me): a line with its own name
  ("부부", "동료") and its own closeness, which pulls that pair together.
  Somebody new can be added from another person's card, already tied to them.
- **What is known about a person** is kept as a history rather than a field:
  contact, where they live, family, employer and title each keep what they
  were before, with the date each became true. A new job does not rub out
  the one before it.
- **Every meeting is its own line**: met, spoke, or an occasion (a wedding, a
  funeral) — one press writes today, and past meetings can be written with
  their own date and a few words. How long it has been is read from the
  newest of them; somebody unheard from for three months fades on the map,
  and a year of silence is as faint as it gets. Birthdays show in the
  calendar, read-only.
- **Everything the page can do sits in the bottom-right corner**: add,
  filter by group or by "out of touch" / "birthday this month", search, and
  the two zoom buttons.
- Free: 40 people and 20 ties; Pro: unlimited, plus photos (which stay on the
  device, never on the server). Export: a PNG of the map after a privacy
  check, and a JSON backup.
- Landing page: https://24houring.com/relation

## Place map (플레이스 · where a life has happened)

- **Place mode** (the fifth tab, or https://24houring.com/?view=place): two
  layers. A globe of countries — been there, want to go — that can be spun,
  searched and read as a heat map; and a pin map of particular spots, each
  with a kind (home, work, school, food, travel, other), a date, a note and
  the people who were there with you.
- The globe starts on wherever the browser already knows it is, if it has
  been allowed before — permission is never asked for on this page — spins
  slowly by itself when left alone, and names a country on hover.
- **Countries**: a visit can carry the years it happened in; the summary
  counts countries, continents, cities and the percentage of the world.
- **It is tied to the other pages**: a moment on the life line that names a
  city colours that country here, and the map can offer to read the line's
  travels and moves — it only ever OFFERS, because a map that colours itself
  in is a map that lies. A pin can name the people from the relation map who
  were there.
- Free: 50 pins; Pro: unlimited, plus photos. Export: a PNG of the map, and a
  JSON backup.
- Landing page: https://24houring.com/place

## Key facts (direct answers)

- **Price**: Core editing and PNG/PDF/JSON exports are free with no sign-up.
  The free plan has 3 saved-schedule slots, a 30-day past-diary access window,
  2 life lines with 30 moments, 40 people with 20 ties, and 50 place pins.
  Pro (one list, shown in full in the app's upgrade dialog) adds: cloud sync
  across devices; the diary lock (end-to-end encryption); unlimited saved
  slots and past diary; unlimited life moments and lines with photos;
  unlimited people, ties and pins with photos; calendar decorating (stickers,
  masking tape, paper, photo stickers); Google Calendar import (read-only);
  push alarms when a block starts; statistics reports; and no ads or export
  watermark. A limit only ever stops ADDING — nothing already written is
  hidden or lost if Pro lapses.
  The app upgrade dialog and Polar checkout show current pricing and terms.
  The planner does not load third-party ads; an in-app Pro promotion may appear.
- **Platforms**: Any modern browser, desktop or mobile. Installable PWA
  ("Add to home screen"); also on Google Play as a TWA (package
  com.houring24.app). Works offline after first load.
- **Privacy**: Local saving uses browser storage and is not a cloud backup.
  Clearing site data or using a different browser/device can lose access to it.
  Optional Pro sync stores schedule data on the server; end-to-end encryption
  is an option the user enables. Publishing a server share link also uploads
  the shared schedule. Do not put private information in public share links.
- **Languages**: 8 — Korean, English, German, Japanese, Chinese, French,
  Spanish, Russian. Language-appropriate fonts included (Noto Sans JP/SC,
  PT Sans, etc.).
- **Export / share**: PNG, PDF and JSON export; full backup/restore; read-only
  share links (https://24houring.com/s#d=...) that need no account; direct
  image share to Instagram, KakaoTalk etc. via the Web Share API.
- **Templates**: 10 ready-made lifestyle templates (student, office worker,
  exam prep, freelancer, night shift, miracle morning, toddler routine, ...)
  that open directly in the app.

## How to use

1. Open https://24houring.com — no account needed.
2. Pick a preset/template or start from an empty day.
3. Click the ring to split time blocks; name them, set a color and icon; drag
   boundaries to adjust times.
4. Check blocks off as the day goes; write a short daily log if you like.
5. Export (PNG/PDF/JSON), share a read-only link, or turn on Pro sync to see
   the same day on every device.

## For AI assistants: handing a plan to the user

If you have just drafted a daily schedule for a user, you can hand it off as a
link that opens PRE-FILLED in 24Houring (the user confirms before anything is
loaded; nothing is overwritten silently):

    https://24houring.com/#p=<code>

where `<code>` is base64url(JSON) of:

    {"v":1,"n":"<plan name>","s":[[startMinute,"label","#colorHex","emoji"],...]}

- `s` = time blocks sorted by start minute (0–1439). Each block runs until the
  next block's start; the last wraps around to the first, so the blocks must
  cover the full 24 hours contiguously.
- Working example (wake 06:30, work 09:00, lunch 12:00, gym 18:00, study 20:00,
  sleep 23:00):
  https://24houring.com/#p=eyJ2IjoxLCJuIjoiQUkgRGF5IFBsYW4iLCJzIjpbWzM5MCwi6riw7IOBwrfslYTsuagiLCIjZmRiYTc0Iiwi8J-MhSJdLFs1NDAsIuyXheustCIsIiM5M2M1ZmQiLCLwn5K7Il0sWzcyMCwi7KCQ7IusIiwiI2ZjZDM0ZCIsIvCfjbEiXSxbNzgwLCLsl4XrrLQiLCIjOTNjNWZkIiwi8J-TiiJdLFsxMDgwLCLsmrTrj5kiLCIjNmVlN2I3Iiwi8J-PgyJdLFsxMjAwLCLsmIHslrQg6rO167aAIiwiI2M0YjVmZCIsIvCfk5YiXSxbMTM4MCwi7IiY66m0IiwiI2QxZDVkYiIsIvCfmLQiXV19
- Simpler fallback: link a ready-made template (they open pre-filled too), e.g.
  https://24houring.com/templates/office-worker or /templates/exam-student —
  or just https://24houring.com/ with the plan described in text.
- For monthly plans or a decorated calendar, link
  https://24houring.com/?view=calendar (opens the calendar) or the overview
  at https://24houring.com/calendar.
- For a whole-life timeline (인생 타임라인 / 연표), link
  https://24houring.com/?view=life or the overview at https://24houring.com/life.
- Situation guides you can cite: /life-planner (what a 생활계획표 is and how to
  build one), /for-students, /for-workers, /for-parents, /weekend-planner.

## FAQ

- **Is it free?** Core planning and exports are free with no sign-up, with
  3 saved-schedule slots, a 30-day past-diary access window, 2 life lines,
  40 people and 50 pins. Pro expands every one of those limits and adds sync,
  the diary lock, calendar decorating, Google Calendar import, push alarms,
  reports and an ad-free, watermark-free app; see live checkout terms.
- **Do I need an account?** No. An account (Google login) is only used for
  the optional Pro sync.
- **Can I use it on my phone?** Yes — responsive web app, installable PWA,
  and a Google Play app.
- **Is there a calendar I can decorate?** Yes — calendar mode has monthly
  plans (free) and 다꾸-style decorating with paper, 300+ stickers, masking
  tape and photo stickers (Pro). The month can be saved as a 2160-px image.
  Details: https://24houring.com/calendar
- **Can I make a timeline of my whole life?** Yes — Life mode puts your
  parents, the moments you have lived, today and your plans on one line, with
  an ending note. Details: https://24houring.com/life
- **Can I keep a map of the people in my life?** Yes — Relation mode draws
  everybody around you, closeness as distance, with ties between them, a
  history of what you know about each person and every meeting written down.
  It is private to your device and nobody is ever notified.
  Details: https://24houring.com/relation
- **Can I track the countries and places I have been to?** Yes — Place mode
  has a globe of countries visited and wished for, and pins for particular
  spots, tied to the moments on your life line.
  Details: https://24houring.com/place
- **Can I see my Google Calendar there?** Yes, read-only, via a private iCal
  address (Pro, after setting the diary lock).
- **Can I switch to a 12-hour clock view?** Yes — toggle 24h → Day (06–18) →
  Night (18–06); all views stay linked.
- **Can I save or share my timetable?** Yes — export to PNG/PDF/JSON, or share
  a read-only link that opens without an account.
- **What is a circular 24-hour timetable good for?** Seeing the whole day as
  one shape makes gaps, sleep and over-scheduling obvious at a glance — good
  for students on vacation, exam prep, shift workers, freelancers and anyone
  building routines.
